column1: # iota(4,11) >= 32 ?  one line per deg(0) cube of the symmetry-broken encoding.
# Written by tools/rung.sh; each line is one `iota_sym --only-deg` invocation.
# The rung is UNSAT only when EVERY cube is UNSAT. A cube marked
# `undecided` carries the budget it was stopped at, per docs/reading.md rule 13.
# SIX OF THESE CUBES ARE PROVABLY EMPTY AND DID NOT NEED SOLVING.
# In a 4-uniform sunflower-free family every point has degree at most
# g(3): the star at a point IS its link, which is 3-uniform, distinct and
# sunflower-free (PureLink.link_at_point_bounded).  PureLink.g_three_at_most_26
# gives g(3) <= 26 unconditionally, so deg(0) >= 27 is impossible and
# cubes 27..32 contain nothing.  They were solved anyway, before this was
# noticed, and cadical returned UNSAT for every one -- which is a cross
# check of the encoding against the kernel rather than wasted work, but
# it was not deliberate.
# With AbbottGardner1969 (g(3) = 20) the empty range widens to 21..32 and
# only deg(0) = 12..20 can hold anything.  That value is a citation, so
# the unconditional statement is the one this file is run against.
# Cube 12 -- the floor, and the one 33.5a expected to be worst -- was
# decided on an Apple M4 Air, not on the session container: RUNG_THREADS=8
# RUNG_SLICE=900, so it stalled at 900 s, split into 19 degree-sequence
# sub-cubes and finished UNSAT at 3236.4 s with none at the limit. That
# is 33.5a's "nineteen sequences" for deficiency four, confirmed. Every
# other row was measured on the container.
# Cubes 15 and 16 were decided on the same M4-class VM, WHOLE -- run with
# RUNG_SLICE=90000 above the 86400 s budget, so the degree-sequence split
# never fired and each is one sequential cadical on one core.
# THE WHOLE-CUBE COST CURVE -- AND THE FIT THAT WAS WRONG.
# An earlier version of this header fitted a log-linear curve to the
# three points 17/16/15, got 2.89x per step down, and predicted
# deg(0)=14 came in at 51305.5 s. The prediction was HIGH BY 1.92x, and
# the ratio broke from ~2.9x to 1.47x, so the curve is not geometric and
# the fit's form was wrong rather than merely imprecise. THE 79 h FIGURE
# FOR deg(0)=13 IS WITHDRAWN; three measured ratios that do not agree
# with each other cannot support a fourth.
# What was said instead, before 13 was run: its cost is unknown, and the
# one structural fact nearby is that the number of admissible degree
# sequences falls sharply as deg(0) does -- 1045128 at 16, 238850 at 15,
# 32797 at 14, 1949 at 13, 19 at 12 -- while the whole-cube time rose
# from 16 to 14. Whether that trend continues to 13 is exactly what is
# not known.
# IT DID CONTINUE, MILDLY. deg(0)=13 came in at 85123.9 s (23.65 h),
# a ratio of 1.66x over 14 -- close to 14's 1.47x and nothing like the
# 2.9x the withdrawn fit assumed. A range of 21-44 h was offered before
# the run on the strength of the two shallow ratios rather than a fit;
# it held, near its low end. The lesson stands either way: the four
# measured ratios are 2.72, 3.06, 1.47, 1.66, and no curve through the
# first three would have found the last two.
# WHICH MEANS THE DEGREE-SEQUENCE SPLIT IS THE WRONG TOOL AT deg(0)=13.
# An earlier version of this paragraph put the split at "roughly 597
# core-hours against 79 for the cube whole". Both numbers were wrong: 597
# came from timing the FRONT of a most-extreme-first enumeration, which
# is an ordered prefix and not a sample, and 79 was the very figure
# withdrawn four paragraphs above. Superseded by roadmap 40, which
# sampled uniformly, and now by the cube itself:
#   split, lower bound (1949 sub-cubes, uniform sample of 24, 19
#     reported, 63% censored at the 7200 s cap, mean >= 6161 core-s)
#                                            >= 3336 core-hours
#   cube 13 whole, one core, measured             23.65 core-hours
#   ratio                                              >= 141x
# 3336 is a floor: most of the sample hit the cap, and it was measured
# under 10-way contention that ran the same sub-cubes 2.7-4.0x slower
# than uncontended. The split wins only when it is small: at deg(0)=12 it
# is 19 sub-cubes and it turned an undecided cube into 3236 s.
# AND A KILLED SPLIT LEAVES NOTHING. rung.sh captures the solver's whole
# output in a shell variable, so no sub-cube verdict streams while it
# runs, and it passes no --checkpoint, so none is written either. A split
# run at deg(0)=13 was stopped after five days and yielded zero reusable
# work; the row rung.sh then recorded was the 60.1 s slice stall, whose
# budget column understated the real spend by five days of ten-core time.
# Such a row must be deleted before re-running: the skip test matches the
# deg column alone and ignores the verdict, so it would silently skip the
# cube as already decided.
# So iota_sym's default --cubecap 400 was RIGHT to refuse the split at
# deg(0) = 13 and 14, and session N+11's diagnosis -- that the cap
# carried over from the g=10 rung was the reason those cubes failed --
# was backwards. The cap was the protection, not the bug. Raising it to
# 3000 or 4000 forces a split that costs at least 141x more than not
# splitting.
# THE RUNG IS CLOSED. All twenty-one cubes deg(0) = 12..32 are UNSAT,
# 195146.4 s = 54.2 h of solver time in total. There is no 4-uniform
# intersecting sunflower-free family of 32 members on eleven points:
# What that does and does not settle is in roadmap 43. It closes the
# ELEVEN-POINT ground set, not iota(4), which is a maximum over all
# ground sets; Sharp.AHSOptimal at b = 4 needs 32 SOMEWHERE, and twelve
# points and up are untouched.
# deg0
